questions.question: How did the CATR affinity measured by the two assays on DPC-refolded AAC3 compare, and what did the authors emphasize about the ITC value?

options.A: ITC gave ~15 µM and NMR ~150 µM, both far weaker than membrane AAC3; the ITC value was especially challenged by the nanomolar consensus.
options.B: ITC gave ~150 µM and NMR ~15 µM, agreeing with native membranes.
options.C: Both gave ~15 nM, within the membrane consensus.
options.D: ITC and NMR both gave ~150 µM, matching native AAC3.

questions.rationale: The paper reports an approximately tenfold assay difference and notes that both micromolar estimates are orders of magnitude weaker than membrane binding values.
questions.evidence_quote: To validate the integrity of their refolded protein, the authors first used ITC to measure a Kd of ~15 µM for the binding of CATR to DPC--refolded AAC3. They then determined CATR--dependent chemical shift perturbations by NMR, giving a Kd of ~150 µM.

questions.question: What corrected literature value undermined the comparison used for ATR binding in the work being criticized?

options.A: A reported 192 µM ATR Kd was corrected in an erratum to 192 nM.
options.B: A reported 192 nM value was corrected to 192 µM.
options.C: A 15 µM CATR value was corrected to 1.2 nM.
options.D: A 72 nM value was corrected to 192 nM.

questions.rationale: The authors identify a typographical unit error in the cited Babot et al. value: micromolar should have been nanomolar.
questions.evidence_quote: Yet, the authors only compare their values to a Kd of 192 µM for the binding of ATR taken from one particular study by Babot et al., 2012 6 . Importantly, the µM unit used in this reference was a typographical error and the Kd value has recently been corrected to 192 nM in an erratum 7 .

questions.question: What comparison did the authors use to show that native AAC3 transport is strongly inhibited by CATR?

options.A: ADP transport was half-maximally inhibited at 1.2 nM CATR.
options.B: ADP transport was half-maximally inhibited at 1.2 µM CATR.
options.C: ATP transport was fully inhibited at 72 nM CATR.
options.D: ADP binding had a Kd of 1.2 mM in membrane.

questions.rationale: The cited transport result is a nanomolar inhibition concentration and supports the claimed strong physiological-affinity range.
questions.evidence_quote: In fact, published Kd values for CATR binding to AAC in the membrane are all in the low nanomolar range (Supplementary Table 1 ), consistent with our own measurements that show that ADP transport by AAC3 is half--maximally inhibited by 1.2 nM CATR (Fig. 1a ).

questions.question: What was the mean CATR dissociation constant measured by ITC for native yeast AAC3 purified in maltoside/cardiolipin, and how did the authors qualify the experiment?

options.A: 72 nM; only 2 of 10 trials succeeded because the enthalpic change was low and apo-state unstable.
options.B: 72 µM; all ten trials succeeded easily.
options.C: 15 nM; only one of ten trials succeeded because CATR dissociated rapidly.
options.D: 150 nM; two of ten trials succeeded due to high enthalpy.

questions.rationale: The paper gives an average of 72 nM and explicitly cautions that the measurement was technically difficult, succeeding in only two trials.
questions.evidence_quote: Our ITC measurements using native AAC3 from yeast mitochondria purified in dodecyl-maltoside/tetraoleoyl cardiolipin gave an average Kd of 72 nM (Fig. 1b ), which is 200 to 2000--fold lower than those reported in Brüschweiler et al.. These experiments were very difficult to do (only 2 out of 10 trials succeeded), as the enthalpic change is low and the apo--state is very unstable in detergent 5 .

questions.question: According to the proposed structural explanation, what stabilizes the unliganded carrier’s transmembrane helix bundle in its native setting?

options.A: Lateral membrane pressure opposed by counter-pressure from the water-filled cavity.
options.B: A dense network of inter-domain polar side-chain bonds on the cytoplasmic face.
options.C: Permanent covalent links between the helices and CATR.
options.D: DPC micelles that mimic a bilayer’s lateral pressure.

questions.rationale: The authors say the helix ring is held together largely by membrane lateral pressure and counter-pressure from the internal cavity, explaining detergent vulnerability.
questions.evidence_quote: There are very few polar side chain interactions in AAC3 that stabilize the structure and they are mainly found on the matrix side, where they form intra--domain rather than inter--domain interactions 3 . The ring of transmembrane a-helices is held together largely by the lateral pressure of the membrane and counter pressure from the water--filled cavity (Supplementary Fig. 1a ) 3 , explaining why unliganded AAC3 in detergent micelles is prone to unfolding.

questions.question: What happened in the CPM thermostability assay when native AAC3 was diluted into 3 mM DPC, and what did added CATR do?

options.A: The signal was high without a melt transition, and CATR had no effect, consistent with loss of a functional binding site.
options.B: A typical melt curve appeared and CATR shifted it upward, proving native folding.
options.C: The melt transition moved lower with CATR, indicating tight binding in DPC.
options.D: No fluorescence was detected until CATR was added, indicating refolding.

questions.rationale: Unlike maltoside, DPC produced a high signal with no transition and CATR did not shift it, which the authors interpret as non-native AAC3 lacking functional binding.
questions.evidence_quote: When the same AAC3 preparation was diluted into 3 mM DPC, a high signal was observed with no transition, showing that AAC3 in DPC is in a non--native state (Fig. 1d ). In this case, CATR addition had no effect, demonstrating that there was no functional binding site.

questions.question: What functional consequence followed dilution of AAC3 into DPC before liposome reconstitution?

options.A: A complete loss of CATR-sensitive ADP uptake, unlike the maltoside-diluted control.
options.B: A twofold increase in CATR-sensitive ADP uptake.
options.C: No uptake in either DPC or maltoside controls.
options.D: CATR-insensitive uptake that recovered after 48 hours.

questions.rationale: The uptake comparison is a direct functional test: DPC pretreatment abolished the inhibitor-sensitive transport seen in the maltoside control.
questions.evidence_quote: Consistent with these findings, dilution of AAC3 into DPC before reconstitution resulted in a complete loss of CATR--sensitive ADP uptake in liposomes, in contrast to control tests where the protein was diluted into dodecyl--maltoside prior to reconstitution (Supplementary Fig. 2 ).

questions.question: Why do the authors argue that CATR binding itself stabilizes AAC3 in detergent?

options.A: CATR makes numerous polar and van der Waals contacts that cross-link most transmembrane helices.
options.B: CATR removes the transmembrane helices from the membrane and exposes them to water.
options.C: CATR raises the protein’s isoelectric point, neutralizing membrane destabilization.
options.D: CATR covalently attaches AAC3 to cardiolipin.

questions.rationale: The proposed mechanism is ligand-mediated helix cross-linking through many interactions, producing both high affinity and increased detergent stability.
questions.evidence_quote: Binding of CATR introduces a large number of polar and van der Waals interactions, which cross--link most of the transmembrane α--helices of AAC3 together 3, 17 , explaining the high affinity of CATR for AAC3 as well as the improved stability in detergents

questions.question: What discrepancy did the authors identify for ADP binding measured by NMR on refolded AAC3?

options.A: The 500 μM value was about 85-fold above membrane consensus and 25-fold above the solubilized-carrier value.
options.B: The 500 nM value was about 85-fold below membrane consensus.
options.C: The 500 μM value matched the solubilized carrier but was 25-fold below membrane consensus.
options.D: The 150 μM value was 85-fold above membrane consensus and 25-fold below the native protein.

questions.rationale: The paper explicitly quantifies the difference of the NMR-derived 500 μM ADP Kd relative to membrane and solubilized reference values.
questions.evidence_quote: We also note that the Kd of ADP binding determined by NMR (500 μM) 1 is ~85--fold higher than the published consensus values of the carrier in the mitochondrial membrane and ~25--fold higher than for the solubilized carrier (Supplementary Table 2 ).

questions.question: Which caveat about interpreting NMR chemical-shift perturbations did the authors raise given AAC3’s charge and the ligands’ charge?

options.A: At high ligand concentrations and temperatures, shifts could reflect nonspecific electrostatic interactions with positively charged AAC3.
options.B: The shifts must reflect covalent ligand attachment because AAC3 is negatively charged.
options.C: The shifts cannot arise nonspecifically because ADP and CATR are neutral at physiological pH.
options.D: The shifts establish binding at the central cavity despite all assigned residues being elsewhere.

questions.rationale: AAC3 has pI 9.82 and is highly positive, whereas CATR, ADP and ATP are negative at neutral pH; the authors warn that concentrated ligand could cause nonspecific interactions.
questions.evidence_quote: AAC3 has an isoelectric point of 9.82, meaning that it is highly positively charged, whereas CATR and the substrates ADP and ATP are negatively charged molecules at neutral pH. The chemical shift perturbations could represent non--specific interactions of CATR or ADP with AAC3 promoted by the high concentrations and temperatures used in these NMR experiments.
